fx-salary-delay.summary: Your salary delay shifts the cash inflow to after the SIP debit date, so you should verify timing and available balance.

A salary delay changes only the timing of cash flow, not the monthly amounts; it does not guarantee the SIP debit will succeed.
If the bank account lacks sufficient balance on the SIP date, the debit may be missed, and consecutive missed instalments could lead the fund house to stop further debits.

fx-failure.summary: A SIP debit failure can occur for several reasons, and understanding the process helps you know what to verify.

points.text: The fund house may stop debiting your account after one or more missed installments, but there is no penalty for the missed SIP.
If two or three consecutive installments are missed, the fund house may halt further debits and return any unused post‑dated cheques.
A common cause of a failed debit is insufficient balance in the linked bank account on the scheduled date.
Another possible cause is an issue with the bank mandate (e.g., NACH authorization) that allows the fund house to pull the amount.

missing_information: The specific reason why the debit failed for this instance
The status of the bank mandate and any bank‑level notifications
next_steps: Check that your bank account has enough available balance on the SIP date ({sip_date}).
Verify that the direct‑debit/NACH mandate for the SIP is active and not revoked by your bank.
Review any communication from the mutual fund house about a possible temporary stop of the SIP after missed installments.
fx-failure.uncertainty: LifeFlow cannot determine the exact cause of the failure without bank or mandate details.

fx-mandate.summary: A mandate is the authorisation you give to debit your bank account for each SIP instalment.

points.text: The SIP mandate is an application form where you specify the date and amount for the recurring investment.
It enables automatic monthly debits through standing instructions, electronic clearing service or post‑dated cheques.
Once set, the mandate allows the fund house to pull the pre‑determined amount each month without you needing to write a cheque each time.

next_steps: Review the SIP mandate form you filled to confirm the chosen date and amount.
Ensure your bank account has sufficient balance on the chosen SIP date.
fx-mandate.uncertainty: This explanation is based on general educational sources and may not reflect the exact process of every fund house.

fx-missed-instalment.summary: Missing an SIP installment does not incur a penalty, but the fund house may stop further debits.

points.text: If you miss one SIP installment, there is no penalty; the mutual fund company may simply stop the SIP, so future installments won’t be debited.
If two or three installments are missed consecutively, the fund house may stop processing post‑dated cheques or halt debits altogether, still without any penalty or forfeiture.

next_steps: Check your bank account balance to ensure sufficient funds for future SIP dates.
Review the terms of your SIP mandate in your mutual fund portal or statement.
fx-missed-instalment.uncertainty: Specific fund houses may have slight variations in how they handle missed installments, which is not captured here.
